This R markdown prepares data and figures contained within the report, Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment for Water Supplies at Cedar Breaks National Monument.

### 1. Setup the workspace

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = TRUE)

#load("data/park/CEBR/CEBR_report_data.RData")

# Load functions after park files in case functions were updated since last save.
source('setup.R')

mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE, 
               georaster = FALSE, 
               basemaps = c("Esri.WorldTopoMap",
                            "Esri.WorldImagery"))

pal <- list(
  black = "black", 
  gold = "#dca237", 
  lightblue = "#6eb2e4", 
  teal = "#459a74", 
  yellow = "#eee461", 
  darkblue = "#3070ad", 
  orange = "#c66426", 
  pink = "#c07da5",
  lightpink = "#ECD8E4"
)

nps_pal <-list(blue = "#85b6dc", 
               red = "#c5312a", 
               grey = "#a9a9a9", 
               lightgrey = "#dcdcdc")

# define conversions
gal_to_cf <- 0.133681

```

Define park using 4-digit NPS Unit Code. Codes for all parks can be found at: <https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/upload/NPS-Unit-List.xlsx>.

Download the park boundary from the NPS IRMA DataStore as an {sf} object.

```{r park_dat}
park <- "CEBR"

# Get park geometry and metadata
park_boundary <- getParkBoundary(park = park)
state <- park_boundary$STATE

```

### 2. Identify the water supplies

A water supply system database was created for this project using various NPS and public databases. The database contains a row for each water supply system and source of water (e.g., individual wells, diversions, and springs) associated with each supply. Here, we also bring in locations of sites that were sampled during a July 2025 site visit, spring locations from a 2023 trip report, and the Spring Stewardship Institute springs that are mapped in the area.

```{r}
# Directory
table_path <- "data/Water_Supply_Systems/NPS_Water_Systems_Database_Joined.xlsx"

# Import table with water supply source locations and filter to CEBR
source_table_locs <- read_excel(table_path, sheet = 1, na = "NA", skip = 1) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::filter(park_unit == park,
                    !source_type %in% c("hauled","Hauled")) %>%
     drop_na(c("source_longitude", "source_longitude")) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = (c("source_longitude","source_latitude")),
           crs = 4326,
            remove = FALSE) 

```

# 3. Load supplementary datasets

With our water supplies identified, we now pull in other relevant datasets that we'll use to characterize the source area and contributing area.

#### - Springs

Here, we load in springs that were sampled during a July 2025 site visit, a september 2023 site visit, and from the Spring Stewardship Institute database (SSI).

```{r springs_load}

samp_locs <- 
  read_csv(
    "data/park/ZION/site_visit/2025_July_Zion_CEBR_PIPE_Sampling_Summary.csv") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(park == "CEBR") %>%
  # Assign elevation to points using {elevatr} package
  get_elev_point(src = "aws", z = 14)

# Spring locations were available in a 2023 September 23 Trip Report Document
springs <- read_csv("data/park/CEBR/springs.csv") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  drop_na(utm_n_12_s) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("utm_e_12s", "utm_n_12_s"), crs = 26912) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(description = as.character(description)) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Import springs from the spring stewardship institute database
SSI_springs <- read_csv("data/park/ZION/SSI_SW_Utah.csv") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude_dd","latitude_dd"), crs = 4326)

```

#### - Watersheds

Get watershed associated with the water supply point and other watersheds that overlap the park.

```{r watersheds}

# Delineate the watershed 
source_table_locs <- source_table_locs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(watershed = 
                  purrr::map(.x = 1:nrow(.),
                             .f = ~ getXYWatersheds(sf = source_table_locs[.x,], 
                                                    coordinates = NULL, 
                                                    snap = FALSE)))

all_watersheds <- getAOIWatersheds(aoi = park_boundary)

# Plot - 
mapview(all_watersheds, col.regions = "seagreen") +
mapview(source_table_locs$watershed) 
```

#### - Geology

There are a few geology datasets available for CEBR. Here, we load a geology geodatabase that was prepared by NPS for CEBR:

NPS Geology for CEBR: 2022. Digital Geologic-GIS Map of Cedar Breaks National Monument and Vicinity, Utah (NPS, GRD, GRI, CEBR, CEBR digital map) adapted from a Utah Geological Survey Map by Biek, Rowley, Anderson, Maldonado, Moore, Hacker, Eaton, Hereford, Sable, Filkorn and Matyjasik (2015). National Park Service (NPS) Geologic Resources Inventory (GRI) program <https://irma.nps.gov/DataStore/Reference/Profile/2293738>

#### - Weather Stations

Pull in NOAA weather stations near the park

```{r}
library(rnoaa)

#get weather data for all stations (depending on dates and how many stations this can take a while)
noaa <- getNOAA(st_buffer(park_boundary, 10000), "CEBR") %>% 
  st_transform(4326)

# Get list of stations with geospatial attributes
stations <- noaa %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(1) %>% # Keep the first row within each group
  ungroup()

# Tidy data
weather_data <- noaa %>%
  dplyr::select(name, date, prcp, snow, snwd, tmax, tmin, tobs) %>%
  # info stored as data * 10 for these params... so reconvert:
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin", "prcp"), function(x) {x * 0.10}) %>%
  # convert from mm to inches
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("snow","snwd", "prcp"), function(x) {x * 0.0393701}) %>%
  # convert from Celsius to Fahrenheit
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax","tmin"), function(x) {(9/5) * x + 32})

rm(noaa)

# Summarize to monthly
weather_data_mon <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7)),
                Date = date,
                year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax = max(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin = min(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax,tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Date = ym) %>%
   addWaterYear() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(waterYear, name) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(prcp_cum = cumsum(prcp),
                   snow_cum = cumsum(snow),
                   snwd_cum = cummax(snwd),
                melt = snow_cum-snwd) # THis might be a stretch, but, technically,
                                      # cumulative snow fall minus current snow
                                      # depth should equal melt. Cumulative snow
                                      
# Summarize to annual
weather_data_an <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Date = date,
                year = year(date),
                waterYear = calc_water_year(date, water_year_start_month = 7)) %>%
  #addWaterYear() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year, name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax,tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE)) 

# Extract data for blowhard mtn station specifically for statistics
# don't include first and last year (1964 and 2006) because they are incomplete
blowhard_mtn_d <- weather_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "BLOWHARD MTN RADAR") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tmean = (tmin + tmax)/2,
                snwd_int = na.approx(snwd)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(snowless_days = ifelse(snwd_int < 1,1,0),
                warm_days = ifelse(tmax > 60, 1, 0))

blowhard_mtn_m <- blowhard_mtn_d %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax,tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd = max(snwd_int, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snowless_days = sum(snowless_days, na.rm = TRUE),
                   warm_days = sum(warm_days, na.rm = TRUE)) 

blowhard_mtn_an <- blowhard_mtn_d %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 1964 & year < 2006) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax,tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd = max(snwd_int, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snowless_days = sum(snowless_days, na.rm = TRUE),
                   warm_days = sum(warm_days, na.rm = TRUE)) 


# Print statistics summary for Blowhard Mtn station
print(blowhard_mtn_d %>% summary())

# Identify other nearby stations
select_station_list <- c("BLOWHARD MTN RADAR","CEDAR BREAKS NM", 
                         "CEDAR BREAKS STORAGE", "LOWDER RANGER STATION")

# Show that blowhard station is a little higher elev than other stations
mapview(stations %>% dplyr::filter(name %in% select_station_list) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(elevation = elevation / .3048), # m to ft
        zcol = "elevation",
        layer.name = "Weather Station Elevation (ft)")

# Plot blowhard mountain station along with a few other nearby stations
p1 <- ggplot(weather_data_mon %>% dplyr::filter(name %in% select_station_list),
       aes(x = ym, y = prcp, color = name)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
    scale_color_manual("", values = c(pal$lightblue, pal$pink, "seagreen", "tomato")) +
  #geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() 


ggarrange(p1,
          p1 + xlim(as.Date("1965-01-01"), as.Date("1972-01-01")) +
            labs(title = "Overlap Period:"),
          ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE)

# Plot of annual blowhard mtn data only
ggplot(blowhard_mtn_d %>% pivot_longer(#cols = c("tmax","tmin","tmean","prcp","snow","snwd"), 
                                       cols = c("snwd_int"),
                                       names_to = "vars", values_to = "vals"),# %>%
         #dplyr::filter(! vars %in% c("tmax","tmin","tmean", "snwd")), 
       aes(x = date, y = vals, color = vars)) + 
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual precipitation (in)") +
  scale_color_colorblind() +
  facet_wrap(~vars, scales = "free")

```

#### - SNOTEL

Read in nearby SNOTEL sites and download and compare data to weather station.

```{r snotel}

snotel <- getSNOTEL(aoi = park_boundary, dist = 5000, years = "all") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  st_transform(4326)

snotel_sites <- snotel %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

mapview(snotel_sites)

snotel_tidy <- snotel %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::filter(sensor_id %in% c("PREC.I", "SNWD.I", "WTEQ.I")) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, name, value, sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date, name, sensor_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
                   water_year = mean(water_year, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date, name) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sensor_id, values_from = value) %>% 
  clean_names()

snotel_m <- snotel_tidy %>%
  plyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(snwd = max(snwd_i),
                   prec = max(prec_i),
                   wteq = max(wteq_i))

snotel_an <- snotel_tidy %>%
  #plyr::mutate(wateryear = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(water_year, name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(snwd = max(snwd_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   prec = max(prec_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   wteq = max(wteq_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(swe_frac = wteq/prec)


snotel_an %>% filter(name == "Brian Head") %>% summary()

ggplot(snotel_tidy %>%
         dplyr::filter(water_year > 2013)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = date, y = prec_i, fill = "Precip."), alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = date, y = wteq_i, fill = "SWE"), alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c(pal$darkblue, pal$orange, pal$lightblue))

ggplot(snotel_an %>%
         dplyr::filter(water_year > 2013)) +
#  geom_col(aes(x = water_year, y = prec, fill = "Precip."), alpha = 0.5) + 
 # geom_col(aes(x = water_year, y = wteq, fill = "SWE"), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = water_year, y = swe_frac, color = name)) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~name) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c(pal$darkblue,pal$lightblue))
 

rm(snotel)

```

#### - NWIS Surface Water

For many parks, the nearest USGS stream gage is far away. Therefore, here we pull in all NWIS gages within 100 km of the park boundary. Of those, we only select stream gages that are considered "reference" gages in the [GAGES-II database (Falcone, 2011)](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70046617). We then select the gage that is closest to the park with the most complete period of record and delineate its associated watershed using the `get_nldi_basin()` function from the {nhdplusTools} package.

```{r nwis, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# Get all NWIS sites
nwis <- listNWIS(aoi = park_boundary, dist = 30000) 

########################## Surface Water #######################################

# Get NWIS Stream Gages - Note, this removes all relevant gages for CEBR so not
# adhering to reference gages only.
ref_gages <- get_gagesII(id = unique(nwis$site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(class == "Ref")

# Select by maximum record and distance from supply site
nwis_select_stream_gage <- nwis %>%
  dplyr::filter(#site_no %in% ref_gages$staid,
                data_type_cd == "dv",
                code %in% c("00060", "00054")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(site_no %in% c(#"10241800",
                               "10242000",
                               "10173450"))

# Get watersheds associated with nearest stream gages
nwis_select_watershed <- nwis_select_stream_gage$site_no %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(~ nldi_finder(site_no = .)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sf::st_drop_geometry(nwis_select_stream_gage), 
                   by = "site_no") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(drain_sqkm = st_area(geometry) %>% 
                  set_units("km^2") %>% 
                  as.numeric())

# Load NHD flowlines and filter for specific reaches within the watershed. We
# will use these to select subsets of the alluvium for a volume analysis.
park_flowlines <- park_boundary %>%
  st_buffer(4000) %>%
  dplyr::summarize() %>%
  mapNHDPlusHR() 

#watersheds <- getWatersheds(aoi = st_buffer(park_boundary, 10000))


mammoth_creek_watershed <- nldi_finder(site_no = 10173450)
sevier_watershed <- nldi_finder(site_no = 10174500)
navajo_lake <- nldi_finder(site_no = 10173800)
coal_creek_watershed <- nldi_finder(site_no = 10242000)
north_fork_virgin_watershed <- nldi_finder(site_no = 371705112565001)
duck_creek_watershed <- data.frame(name = "duck_creek",
                         long = c(-112.65649),
                         lat = c(37.52964)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long","lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  getXYWatersheds(sf = ., snap = TRUE)


mapview(mammoth_creek_watershed %>% dplyr::mutate(name = "Mammoth Creek"),
        zcol = NULL,
        col.regions = pal$lightblue,
        layer.name = "Mammoth Creek") +
  #mapview(sevier_watershed) +
  mapview(coal_creek_watershed %>% dplyr::mutate(name = "Coal Creek"),
          zcol = NULL,
          col.regions = pal$orange,
          layer.name = "Coal Creek") +
  #mapview(north_fork_virgin_watershed) +
#  mapview(duck_creek_watershed,
#          col.regions = pal$darkblue,
#          layer.name = "Duck Creek") +
mapview(park_boundary, alpha.regions = 0, lwd = 4, layer.name = "CEBR", col.regions = "black") +
  mapview(source_table_locs,
          col.regions = "black",
          layer.name = "Blowhard Spring") + 
  mapview(all_watersheds, col.regions = "pink")




# Download data from reference stream sites
nwis_select_discharge <- 
  dataRetrieval::readNWISdv(siteNumbers = nwis_select_stream_gage$site_no,
                                                   parameterCd = '00060') %>% # IF WE ALSO WANT HEIGHT == '00065'
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::rename("discharge" = "X_00060_00003",
                "date" = "Date") %>%
  #dplyr::filter(year(date) >= 1940) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(st_drop_geometry(nwis_select_watershed), by = "site_no") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(discharge_in_nwis = 86400 * 12 * discharge / (drain_sqkm * 1.076e+7))


nwis_select_discharge_an <- nwis_select_discharge %>%
  dplyr::mutate(y = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(y, site_no) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_discharge = mean(discharge, na.rm = TRUE),
                   mean_discharge_in_nwis = mean(discharge_in_nwis, na.rm = TRUE),
                   peak_discharge = max(discharge, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "keep")


```

#### - NWIS Groundwater

We also look at NWIS groundwater sites near the park

```{r nwis_gw}

nwis_groundwater <- nwis %>%
  dplyr::filter(data_type_cd == "gw",
                n_obs >= 1) %>%
  add_gw_meta()

mapview(nwis_groundwater)

# There are no groundwater sites right near the park, but several are located below the breaks northwest of Cedar City and to the East on the Markagunt Plateau at lower elevation. To further investigate groundwater levels in the Claron, we now filter to just include wells in the claron (formerly called the Wasatch and labeled in this database as such).

# Pull gw levels in the claron
nwis_claron <- nwis_groundwater %>%
  dplyr::filter(`Local Aquifer Name` == "Wasatch Formation")

mapview(nwis_claron) +
  mapview(park_boundary, alpha.region = 0, color = "black", lwd = 3)

# pull those sites groundwater level data and convert to monthly mean
nwis_groundwater_levels <- dataRetrieval::readNWISgwl(nwis_claron$site_no) %>%
  data.table::data.table() %>%
  dplyr::filter(parameter_cd %in% c(62611, 72019),
                year(as.Date(lev_dt)) >= 1900) %>% # 72019 = depth, 62611 = elevation
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(lev_dt, 1, 7))) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(ym, site_no, parameter_cd) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_lev = mean(sl_lev_va, na.rm. = TRUE), # elevation
                   mean_depth = mean(lev_va, na.rm. = TRUE), # depths
                   .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, site_no, mean_lev, mean_depth) %>%
```

#### - Points of diversion (PODs)

Park water supplies may be sourced from within or beyond the park boundary. This chunk pulls in state-reported water supply locations that occur within a buffer distance of the park boundary. Then, PODs are filtered to identify specific PODs associated with park water supplies. For some parks, the water supply system ID is linked using the water supply database. For others, we assume the water supply is any POD owned by NPS within the selected buffer.

For Utah, the POD_state has an "OWNER" column and NPS is identified by string "NATIONAL PARK". For future states, this is modified.

```{r}
# Now, get state specific points of diversion (POD) (i.e., water supply points)
# EDIT NOTE - Eventually nest into a getPODall function with aoi and dist
# args which then applies the state-specific function.

# Set distance and AOI for POD search
buffer_dist <- 5000 # in meters

aoi <- 
  park_boundary 

# Dictionary to map POD functions to states
POD_dict <- c(
  "CA" = getPODCalifornia,
  "CO" = getPODColorado,
  "MT" = getWaterRightsMontana,
  "NV" = getPODNevada,
  "UT" = getPODUtah
)

# Assign POD_state using the condition map
if (state %in% names(POD_dict)) {
  
  POD_state <- POD_dict[[state]](aoi, buffer_dist)  # Pass additional arguments
  
} else {
  
  print("No PODs returned.")
  
}

# Filter using water supply database to identify PODs associated park water 
# supplies. If table does not have adequate information, select by POD
# owner and location metadata
if(source_table_locs %>% drop_na(state_water_rights_id) %>% nrow() > 0) {
  
  POD_supply <- POD_state %>%
    #dplyr::filter(WRNUM %in% c("61-893", "2061001M00")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(WRNUM %in% source_table_locs$state_water_rights_id) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(LOCATION, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      name = source_table_locs %>% 
        pull (water_system_name)) 
  
} else {
  
  POD_supply <- POD_state %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      OWNER %like% "NATIONAL PARK",
      str_detect(SUMMARY_ST, "A|P")) %>% # approved / perfected applications
    #str_detect(USES,"D|M|O|I")) %>%  # filter by POD use category
    dplyr::distinct(WRNUM,
                    .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(name = source)
}

# All PODS within park
POD_all <- 
  POD_state %>% 
  dplyr::filter(park_right == "Park") %>% 
  dplyr::distinct(WRNUM, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Placeholder layers
mapview(POD_state,
        #zcol = "CFS",
        layer.name = "State Reported PODs",
        homebutton = FALSE,
        cex = 3,
        col.regions = "#6eb2e4") +
  mapview(POD_supply,
          layer.name = "Supply POD",
          homebutton = FALSE,
          cex = 5,
          col.regions = pal$yellow) +
  mapview(source_table_locs,
          layer.name = "Blowhard Spring",
          homebutton = FALSE,
          col.regions = c("tomato"),
          cex = 4) + 
  mapview(park_boundary,
          col.regions = "forestgreen",
          alpha.regions = 0.2,
          homebutton = FALSE,
          legend = FALSE) 
```

# 4. Begin Analysis

#### - Delineate high-elevation recharge area

Blowhard Spring emerges along a North-South trending fault in high-elevation areas near Blowhard Mountain. Notably, just north and west of the spring is the cliff face of the breaks that mark the edge of the Markagunt plateau. The fault is thought to provide a conduit for water to emerge at the spring, however, even if the fault is delivering water, a pressure source is required to raise water to the elevation of Blowhard Spring. The only viable option is a higher elevation recharge area. Here, we map all areas within a 7km buffer of Blowhard Spring that are higher in elevation than the spring outlet. These are considered to be potential recharge areas for the Spring. Spangler (2012) suggests that groundwater is flowing to the North in this area based on dye tracer tests. Therefore, we highlight areas to the south of the spring that are most likely to serve as a recharge area.

```{r elev_data}

# Get elvation using elevatr package
park_elev <- get_elev_raster(source_table_locs %>% st_buffer(7000), z = 14)  %>% 
  rast() %>% 
  terra::project(., st_crs(source_table_locs)$proj4string)

# Extract elevation at Blowhard Spring point
spring_elev <- terra::extract(park_elev, source_table_locs, method = "bilinear")[[2]]

# Select all higher elevation areas that surpass the spring_elev threshold
thresh_elev <- park_elev
thresh_elev[thresh_elev <= spring_elev] <- NA
thresh_bin <- ifel(!is.na(thresh_elev), 1, NA)
names(thresh_elev) <- "Elevation"

# Extract areas as polygons rather than just the original raster
thresh_poly <- as.polygons(thresh_bin, dissolve = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON")

# Select the area to the south that is the most likely recharge zone - this is polygon number 9
recharge_area <- thresh_poly[9,]

#saveRDS(recharge_area, "data/park/CEBR/Climate_Data/recharge_area.rds")
#recharge_area <- readRDS("data/park/CEBR/Climate_data/recharge_area.rds")

# Plot 
mapview::mapviewOptions(basemaps = c("Esri.WorldTopoMap"))# "Esri.WorldImagery"))
mapview(recharge_area, col.regions = "dodgerblue", layer.name = "Recharge Area") #+
#  mapview(thresh_poly, col.regions = "dodgerblue", alpha.regions = 0.2, layer.name = "High-Elevation Area")



# Plot high recharge elevation as raster - takes a min
#my_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("lightblue","darkblue"))(100)

#mapview(thresh_elev, 
#        col.regions = my_colors, 
#        layer.name = "Elevation > 3145 m",
#        alpha.regions = .5,
#        na.color = NA) +
#  mapview(source_table_locs,
#          layer.name = "Blowhard Spring",
#          col.regions = "red") #+


```

#### - Sinkhole detection

Julie Bahr at NPS WRD provided two options exist for sinkhole detection. She described her methods in an email dated June 18, 2025:

"I filled the DEM and subtracted the original DEM from that to get a raster layer representing depth. I then extracted pixels that had a depth value of 5 m or greater and converted them to polygons (CEBR_5m.shp). For the other option, I extracted pixels that had a depth value of 1 m or greater, converted them to polygons, and filtered those polygons to isolate ones that had an area of 100 m² or greater to remove a lot of the smaller features (CEBR_1m_100m.shp). So, basically, there’s two options for filtering the data: we can choose both a depth value and a polygon/surface area value to use to filter the sinkholes depending on what features you’d like to capture.

Additionally, I created a topographic position index (TPI) map, which isn’t the best for extracting the sinkholes as polygons, but can be helpful for visualizing their locations. TPI is a simple calculation based on elevation differences within a defined neighborhood (I chose 50 m) and it seems like USGS frequently uses it to identify sinkholes. I’ve included a screenshot of what that map looks like since I’d need to use my home internet to email you the actual raster file before next week."

```{r}

sinkhole_5m <- read_sf("data/park/CEBR/CEBR_sinkholes/CEBR_5m.shp")

sinkhole_1m <- read_sf("data/park/CEBR/CEBR_sinkholes/CEBR_1m_100m.shp")

sinkhole_1m_centroids <- sinkhole_1m %>% st_centroid()

mapview(thresh_elev, 
        col.regions = my_colors, 
        layer.name = "Elevation > 3145 m",
        alpha.regions = .5,
        na.color = NA) +
mapview(park_boundary, col.regions = "seagreen", alpha.regions = 0.5) +
mapview(sinkhole_1m, col.regions = "yellow", layer.name = "1m sinkhole") +
mapview(sinkhole_5m, col.regions = "orange", layer.name = "5m sinkhole") +
  mapview(sinkhole_1m %>% st_centroid(), col.regions = "red", cex = 3, layer.name = "1m centroids") +
  mapview(source_table_locs,
          layer.name = "Blowhard Spring") +
  mapview(springs[,1:2])


b + mapview(sinkhole_1m %>% st_centroid(), 
            col.regions = "darkblue", 
            cex = 3,
            layer.name = "Sinkholes") +
 mapview(thresh_poly, col.regions = "lightblue")

```

#### - Stable Water Isotopes

Deuterium and Delta-Oxygen-18 can be used to differentiate sources of water based on isotopic signatures of source waters. Precipitation for a given area can have distinct isotopic signatures based on fraction effects from evaporation and continental effects that preferentially vaporize or rain-out lighter and heavier molecules. In high-elevation regions, seasonal variations in isotopic ratios can also reveal season recharge processes for aquifers, with snowmelt often reflecting cooler temperatures found at higher elevations with more negative isotopic signatures. Existing isotope data exists for the area surrounding cedar breaks, including samples from various springs and a nearby precipitation gauge. Here, we plot existing data.

Note: we plan to update this plot with data collected during the July 2025 site visit.

```{r isotopes}

isotopes <- read_csv("data/park/ZION/isotope.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = Location,
                label = str_replace_all(label, 
                    fixed("(C-36- 9)35dca-S1"),"Arch Spring"
                    ))
                #label = factor(label),
                #Sample_Type = factor(Sample_Type))

iso_p <- isotopes %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Lat_dd_WGS, Long_dd_WGS, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Long_dd_WGS", "Lat_dd_WGS"))

mapview(springs[,1], col.regions = "tomato") +
  mapview(iso_p, col.regions = "dodgerblue")

cedar_city_lmwl <- lm(delta_2H ~ delta_18O, data = isotopes %>% dplyr::filter(label == "Cedar City(Utah)"))
cc_slope = cedar_city_lmwl$coefficients[[2]]
cc_int = cedar_city_lmwl$coefficients[[1]]
g_slope <- 8.02
g_int <- 9.47
lab_x <- -7.5


ggplot(isotopes %>% 
         dplyr::filter(#Park_Code == "CEBR",
                       label != "Cedar City(Utah)",
                       Sample_Type %in%  "GWS"), 
       aes(x = delta_18O, y = delta_2H)) +
 
  geom_abline(intercept = g_int, slope = g_slope, show.legend = TRUE, color = "gray80") +
  annotate("text", x = lab_x, y = g_slope * lab_x + g_int +1.7, label = "GMWL",              
           color = "gray40", angle = 30, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
geom_abline(intercept = cc_int, slope = cc_slope, show.legend = TRUE, color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = lab_x, y = cc_slope * lab_x + cc_int - 2.5, label = "LMWL (Cedar City)",              
           color = "black", angle = 30, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
   geom_point(aes(shape = Park_Code), size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
   geom_point(data = isotopes %>% dplyr::filter(Park_Code == "CEBR",
                                    label %in% c("Arch Spring",
                                                 "Cedar Breaks VC tap water",
                                                 "Sunset Spring; CEBR_S0001")), 
              aes(x = delta_18O, y = delta_2H, color = label), shape = 1, size = 6) +
   geom_point(data = isotopes %>% dplyr::filter(Park_Code == "CEBR",
                                    label %in% c("Arch Spring",
                                                 "Cedar Breaks VC tap water",
                                                 "Sunset Spring; CEBR_S0001")), 
              aes(x = delta_18O, y = delta_2H, color = label), size = 2) +
  theme_bw()  +
  labs(
    color = "", # Explicitly name the 'color' legend
    shape = "Sample Type",
    x = expression(delta^{18}*O ~ "(\u2030 vs. VSMOW)"),
    y = expression(delta^{2}*H ~ "(\u2030 vs. VSMOW)")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### 5. Climate and Water Balance

#### - GCM Selection

Climate futures were previously compiled for park and Koppen centroids. This data was used to select which of the CMIP5 climate models to use to represent "hot dry" and "warm wet" scenarios. Here, we read in the pre-determined gcm selections.

```{r}

# Read in selected "Hot dry" "Warm Wet" climate futures
centroid_cfs <- data.table::fread('data/parkwide_gcms.csv') %>%
  dplyr::filter(park %in% {{park}},
                CF %in% c("Warm Wet", "Hot Dry")) %>%
  distinct(GCM, .keep_all = TRUE)

# If there is more than one model selection for a CF scenario, grab the more divergent.
if (nrow(centroid_cfs) > 2) {
  if (nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Hot Dry")) > 1) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_min(delta_pr)
  }
  if ((nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Warm Wet")) > 1) ) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_max(delta_pr)
  }
}


# Read in all available gcms
all_cfs <-
  read_delim( "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rossyndicate/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/master/data/general/GCM_skill_by_region.txt" ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Region == "SWR") %>% #,
                #Rank < 19) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-ES.", "HadGEM2-ES365.", GCM),
                GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-CC.", "HadGEM2-CC365.", GCM)) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(data.table(RCP = c("rcp45","rcp85"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM,RCP)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Skill = ifelse(Rank > 18, "Low Skill", "High Skill"))
  

# GCMs available on amazon web services water balance model gridded datasets.

      "inmcm4",
```

#### - Run WBM

We use the NPS water balance model (WBM) to calculate water budget components. The model requires temperature and precipitation inputs, which we've now downloaded for historical and projected periods. The water balance model is adapted from code base developed in NPS's {WaterBalance} package (<https://github.com/CCRP-Adaptation/WaterBalance>).

For our report, we ran the NPS water balance model (WBM) for each GridMET point in the source area. The average soil moisture capacity, elevation, slope, and aspect are used as inputs for each model run. We then aggregate the values to the weighted mean for the recharge area, returning a spatially averaged daily value. We are running the historical and future datasets separately, but use final conditions from the historical as the starting conditions for the future.

```{r wbm_run}

hist_wbm <- run_NPS_WBM_points(points = clim_pts,
                                         climate_data = clim_hist,
                                         Direct_Frac = 0, # CSU ADDITION
                                         Return_Rate = 1, # CSU ADDITION
                                         PET_Method = "Oudin",
                                         hock_coef = 2,
                                         Snowpack.Init = 0, 
                                         Soil.Init = 0,
                                         Shade.Coeff = 1,
                                         T.Base = 0,
                                         Soil_mult = 1,
                                         PET_mult = 1,
                                         area_weighted = TRUE, 
                                         aoi = recharge_aoi, 
                                         grid = aoi_gridmet_grid,
                                         ret_final_cond = TRUE,
                                         use_final = FALSE) 

fut_wbm <- run_NPS_WBM_points(points = clim_pts,
                                     climate_data = clim_fut,
                                     Direct_Frac = 0, # CSU ADDITION
                                     Return_Rate = 1, # CSU ADDITION
                                     PET_Method = "Oudin",
                                     hock_coef = 2,
                                     Snowpack.Init = 0, 
                                     Soil.Init = 0,
                                     Shade.Coeff = 1,
                                     T.Base = 0,
                                     Soil_mult = 1,
                                     PET_mult = 1,
                                     area_weighted = TRUE, 
                                     aoi = recharge_aoi, 
                                     grid = aoi_gridmet_grid,
                                     ret_final_cond = FALSE,
                                     use_final = TRUE,
                                     param_list = hist_wbm[[2]]) 



recharge_area_ft2 <- recharge_area %>% 
  st_area() %>%
  set_units("ft^2") %>%
  as.numeric()

```

Here, we apply the NPS scenario selection method to identify 4 GCMs that represent "hot dry", "warm dry", "hot wet", and "warm wet" climate scenarios and then, of those, we select the two end members that produce the maximum and minimum runoff, which is the key variable related to water supply.

First calculate differentials (future - baseline) for all climate & WBM data stats

```{r}

# wbm_all pre-routing
wbm_all <- hist_wbm %>%
  #dplyr::select(-c(, discharge_cfs, runoff_cfs_wbm)) %>%
  bind_rows(fut_wbm) %>%
  as.data.table() %>%
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_cfs_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2 / 86400)
  

all_clim_stats <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                stat_period = 
                  ifelse(year < 2013, "Baseline",
                      ifelse(year > 2034 & year < 2065, "Future", "Other"))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Other") %>%
  dplyr::select(GCM, stat_period, Skill, precip_in_wbm, tmean_C, runoff_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm, aet_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, stat_period, Skill) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_precip_in = mean(precip_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   mean_tmean_C = mean(tmean_C),
                   mean_runoff_in = mean(runoff_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   mean_aet_in = mean(aet_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   median_runoff_in = quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75) * 365.25,
                   rel_var_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm - mean(runoff_in_wbm)),
                   sd_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm),
                   cv_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm)/mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   iqr_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75)) - 
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.25)),
                   q90_q10_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.9)) -
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.1)),
                   peak_runoff_in = max(runoff_in_wbm),
                   mean_precip_minus_pet_in = mean(precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm),
                   fract_zero_runoff = sum(runoff_in_wbm == 0) / n() ,
                   .groups = "keep") 


baseline <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period == "Baseline")

future <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Baseline")

future_differentials <- future %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta_precip_in = mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in,
                delta_tmean_C = mean_tmean_C - baseline$mean_tmean_C,
                delta_runoff_in = mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in,
                delta_aet_in = mean_aet_in - baseline$mean_aet_in,
                delta_runoff_rel_var = rel_var_runoff_in - baseline$rel_var_runoff_in,
                fut_runoff_rel_var = rel_var_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_sd = sd_runoff_in - baseline$sd_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_cv = cv_runoff_in - baseline$cv_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_iqr = iqr_runoff_in - baseline$iqr_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_median = median_runoff_in - baseline$median_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_q90_q10 = q90_q10_runoff_in - baseline$q90_q10_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_peak = peak_runoff_in - baseline$peak_runoff_in,
                delta_precip_minus_pet = mean_precip_minus_pet_in - baseline$mean_precip_minus_pet_in,
                delta_fract_zero_runoff = fract_zero_runoff - baseline$fract_zero_runoff) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::select(GCM, CF), by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::rename(c("centroid_cf" = CF)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(centroid_cf = ifelse(centroid_cf %in% c("Hot Dry","Warm Wet"), centroid_cf , 
                            ifelse(Skill == "Low Skill", "Low Skill", "Other"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(RCP = str_sub(GCM, -5))
                          
```

Now, manually select climate future categories

```{r}
selected_cfs <- selected_gcms[[1]] %>%

  data.table() %>%

ggsave(selected_gcms[[2]], filename = "docs/Deep Dives/CEBR/Figs/Climate_Selection.tiff", width = 9, height = 7,  dpi = 600)
```

# 6. Projections

##### - Discharge

```{r discharge_model}

# Manually develop flow model for Blowhard Spring flow using runoff routing
# function.

# Clean data - apply multiplier to runoff
mod_dat <- wbm %>% dplyr::filter(year(date) < 1985) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, runoff_gpm) %>% ungroup() 

springflow <-  runoff_routing_gw(df = mod_dat, 
                                 runoff_col = "runoff_gpm",
                                 date_col = "date",
                                 tau_q = 24, 
                                 tau_s = 68, 
                                 vs = .3,
                                 loss = 0,
                                 baseflow = 0,
                                 delay = 0,
                                 slow_only = TRUE,
                                 return_components = TRUE,
                                 max_inf = 5000) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(blowhard_spr, by = "date")

# Plot of modeled springflow and runoff
ggplot(springflow, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.Date("1983-01-01"), xmax = as.Date("1984-01-01"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  
  geom_line(aes(x = date, y = Q_tot), color = "black", linewidth = 1.5, lineend = "round") + 
  geom_line(aes(x = date, y = Q_tot, color = "Modeled"), linewidth = 1, lineend = "round") + 
  geom_point(aes(y = flow_gpm, color = "Observed"), size = 2, shape = 21, fill = pal$darkblue) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Flow (gpm)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c(pal$lightblue, "black", pal$lightblue))

rm_bd_yrs <- springflow %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!year(date) %in% c(1983)) %>% 
  drop_na(flow_gpm, Q_tot) %>% dplyr::select(flow_gpm, Q_tot)

NSE(sim = rm_bd_yrs$flow_gpm, 
    obs = rm_bd_yrs$Q_tot)

# Fit a linear model of observed vs. predicted values. Remove 1979 - incomplete and boundary year. Remove 1983 - duplicate of 1982.
model <- lm(Q_tot ~ flow_gpm, data = springflow %>% dplyr::filter(!year(date) %in% c(1980, 1983)))

# Get the summary of the model
summary(model)$r.squared

ggplot(springflow %>% dplyr::filter(!year(date) %in% c(1980, 1983)), aes(x = flow_gpm, y = Q_tot)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline() + 
  theme_bw()


### Now - apply model to all water balance years (historical and future)

wbm <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    data.table() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(discharge_gpm = runoff_routing_gw(
                                    df = data.table(date,runoff_gpm),  # The .SD is the subset for the current group
                                    runoff_col = "runoff_gpm",
                                    date_col = "date",
                                    tau_q = 24,
                                    tau_s = 68,
                                    vs = .3,
                                    loss = 0,
                                    baseflow = 0,
                                    delay = 0,
                                    slow_only = TRUE,
                                    return_components = FALSE,
                                    max_inf = 5000
                                  )[,2]) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(discharge_cf = discharge_gpm * 0.133681 * 60 * 24)

#ggplotly(ggplot(wbm, aes(x = date, y = discharge_gpm, color = CF)) + geom_line())

mean_cols <- c("soil_in_wbm", "tmean_C", "runoff_cfs_wbm", "tmean_F", "discharge_gpm")

wbm_annual <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
                #water_year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(Rank, Region, RCP, Skill, date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year,GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(everything(), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

wbm_monthly <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(Rank, Region, RCP, Skill, date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(everything(), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
```

#####- Visitation

Here we pull in park visitation data reported by the NPS and located in NPS IRMA.

```{r}


# Load in historical visitation data

# Get historical monthly reported visitor information
visitors <- getUnitVisitation(units = park, startYear = 1979, endYear = 2024) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(paste0(Year, "-", Month))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = RecreationVisitors + NonRecreationVisitors) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, TotalVisitors) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = ifelse(TotalVisitors == 0,NA, TotalVisitors),
                month = month(ym))

# Summarize monthly NPS visitation to annual sum
visitors_an <- visitors %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(ym, month)) %>%
  dplyr::summarize_all(.funs = sum)

# Create table of monthly mean, max, min, sd, and cv of historical visitors
monthly_visitor_proportions <- visitors %>%
           dplyr::group_by(month) %>%
           dplyr::summarize(TV_mean = mean(TotalVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_max = max(TotalVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_min = min(TotalVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_sd = sd(TotalVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_cv = TV_sd / TV_mean) %>%
           dplyr::mutate(month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-",month,"-01")),
                         fraction = TV_mean/sum(TV_mean))



# Generalized Additive Model - better deals with correlation between year and temp
vis_mod <- mgcv::gam(TotalVisitors ~ year + tmean, 
               data = visitors_an %>%
                      left_join(clim_hist %>% 
                      dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), 
                                    tmean = (tmean_C * 9/5) + 32) %>%
                      dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
                      dplyr::summarize(tmean = mean(tmean),
                                       prcp = mean(ppt_mm)), by = "year"))

# Extract Model Stats# Extract Model Statsprcomp()
r_squared <- summary(vis_mod)$r.sq
p_val <- summary(vis_mod)$p.pv %>% mean()

# Format the equation and R-squared into a single string
vis_r2_label <- paste0("R² = ", format(r_squared, digits = 3))
vis_p_label <- paste0("p = ", format(p_val, digits = 3))

# Prep future climate dataset and use model to project future visitation
vis_clim <- clim_fut %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(GCM %in% selected_cfs$GCM) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, "tmean" = tmean_C) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                tmean = (tmean * 9/5) + 32 ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmean = mean(tmean)) %>%
  bind_rows(vis_mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(year, tmean)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(vis_pred = predict(vis_mod, newdata = ., se.fit = TRUE)$fit,
                vis_pred_SE = predict(vis_mod, newdata = ., se.fit = TRUE)$se.fit,
                vis_pred_low = vis_pred - (vis_pred_SE * 1.96),
                vis_pred_high = vis_pred + (vis_pred_SE * 1.96))

# Because the GAM model predicts year-to-year estimates that vary with temp,
# we then calculate a linear model from the predictions for plots
lin_mod_proj <- lm(vis_pred ~ year, data = vis_clim)
lin_mod_high <- lm(vis_pred_high ~ year, data = vis_clim)
lin_mod_low <- lm(vis_pred_low ~ year, data = vis_clim)

vis_clim <- vis_clim %>%
  dplyr::mutate(vis_pred_lin = predict(lin_mod_proj, newdata = .),
                low_smooth = predict(lin_mod_low, newdata = .),
                high_smooth = predict(lin_mod_high, newdata = .)) %>%
  # Also bind historical visitation
  left_join(visitors_an %>% dplyr::select(year, TotalVisitors), by = "year")

# Monthly vis
proj_vis_sum <- vis_clim %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 2034, year < 2065) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_vis = mean(vis_pred_lin),
                   max_vis = max(high_smooth),
                   min_vis = min(low_smooth)) 

monthly_visitor_proportions <- monthly_visitor_proportions %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fut_min = proj_vis_sum$min_vis * fraction,
                fut_max = proj_vis_sum$max_vis * fraction,
                fut_mean = proj_vis_sum$mean_vis * fraction)


```

```{r}
low_use_per_visitor <- 0.83828345 * 0.133681 # Past use rate (hughes, 1996) [low use]

                low_use_hist = TV_mean * low_use_per_visitor,
                low_use_fut = fut_mean * low_use_per_visitor,
                high_use_hist = TV_mean * high_use_per_visitor,
                high_use_fut = fut_mean * high_use_per_visitor,

                low_use = vis * low_use_per_visitor,

  dplyr::mutate(c_group = ifelse(year <= 2024, "Historical", "Projected"))

                monthly_use_low = use_fraction * low_use) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, monthly_use_low, monthly_use_high, monthly_use_mid) %>%
  full_join(wbm_monthly %>% dplyr::select(ym, discharge_cf, CF), by = "ym")
```

```{r}
# Create table of monthly mean, max, min, sd, and cv of historical visitors
# Note, monthly supply calculated as monthly discharge
monthly_supply_proportions <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::select(CF, date, discharge_cf) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, CF, GCM) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(discharge_cf = sum(discharge_cf, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym),
                        year = year(ym),
                        group = case_when(year <= 2012 ~ "Historical",
                                  #year > 2012 & year < 2025 ~ "Recent Historical",
                                  year > 2034 & year < 2070 ~ "Future",
                                  TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
                  drop_na(group) %>%
           dplyr::group_by(month, CF) %>%
           dplyr::summarize(monthly_supply_cf = mean(discharge_cf, na.rm = TRUE),
                            monthly_supply_cf_max = max(discharge_cf, na.rm = TRUE),
                            monthly_supply_cf_min = min(discharge_cf, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
           dplyr::mutate(month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-",month,"-01")),
                         month_days = days_in_month(month_date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
            dplyr::mutate(total_cf = sum(monthly_supply_cf),
                         monthly_fraction = monthly_supply_cf/total_cf)

monthly_use_long <- monthly_use_proportions %>%
                              #dplyr::select(month_date, mid_use_fut, mid_use_hist, low_use_fut, low_use_hist) %>%
                              pivot_longer(cols = c(mid_use_fut, mid_use_hist, low_use_fut, low_use_hist, high_use_fut, high_use_hist), names_to = "use_cat", values_to = "use_cf") %>%
                              dplyr::mutate(month_date = ifelse(use_cat %in% c("mid_use_hist", "low_use_hist", "high_use_hist"), month_date - years(4), 
                                                                month_date + years(50)),
                                            new_group = ifelse(grepl("low", use_cat), "low_use",
                                                               ifelse(grepl("high", use_cat), "high_use", "mid_use"))) %>%
                              dplyr::select(month_date, new_group, use_cf) %>%
                              group_by(month_date) %>%
                              pivot_wider(names_from = new_group, values_from = use_cf)





# Join annual supply and demand
DS_df <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::select(year, CF, discharge_cf) %>%
```

Fire exposure:

Gao, P., Terando, A. J., Kupfer, J. A., Varner, J. M., Stambaugh, M. C., Lei, T. L., & Hiers, J. K. (2021). Robust projections of future fire probability for the conterminous United States. *Science of The Total Environment, 789*, 147872. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2021.147872>

Fire probability is calculated using a model referred to as PC2FM, which estimates the mean yearly fire interval (MFI). Fire probability is the inverse of MFI (i.e., FP = 1 / MFI). MFI is computed using annual average temperature and precipitation as its primary inputs, as well as factors like molecular collision frequency and activation energy (which influence combustion processes). It is then calibrated using historical fire scar records. Then, future fire probabilities are projected using climate data from the MACAv2 dataset.

```{r exposure}
aoi <- recharge_aoi

water_supply_pyromes <- st_read("data/all/usfs_fire/Pyromes-RDS-2020-0020/Data/Pyromes_CONUS_20200206.shp") %>%
  st_make_valid() %>% 
  sf::st_transform(st_crs(aoi)) %>%
  sf::st_filter(., aoi)

# Cedar Breaksis contained within the Far Southern ROckies pyrom. T
mapview(water_supply_pyromes, zcol = "NAME",
        col.regions = pal$gold, alpha.regions = 0.3) + 
  mapview(park_boundary, col.regions = pal$lightblue) 

# GRAB THE GAO 2021 FIRE PROBABILITY FOR THE APPRORIATE PYROMES AND CLIMATE FUTURES AT BRYCE CANYON:
crosswalk <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021/gcm_crosswalk.csv")

# Back-casted GCMs, compared against GridMet. Really just need GridMet.
fireprob_historic <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021/tables3-fireprob-hist.csv") %>%
  dplyr::select(PYROME, GridMet)

# Midcentury is defined as the avg. across 2040-2070:
all_delta_fireprob <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021//tables12-45-midcentury.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(-PYROME, names_to = "gao") %>%
  left_join(crosswalk, by = "gao") %>%
  mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, ".rcp45")) %>%
  # do same thing on the 85 CFs, then bind together:
  bind_rows(
    read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021//tables6-85-midcentury.csv") %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-PYROME, names_to = "gao", values_to = "value") %>%
      left_join(crosswalk, by = "gao") %>%
      mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, ".rcp85"))
  ) %>%
  # join historic data by pyrome:
  left_join(fireprob_historic, by = "PYROME") %>%
  # Description: "The probability of a fire increases/decreases by `delta_fp` percent." 
  mutate(delta_fp = 100 * ((value - GridMet)/GridMet)) %>%
  left_join(future_differentials, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::filter(PYROME %in% water_supply_pyromes$PYROME)

delta_fireprob <- all_delta_fireprob %>%
  filter(GCM %in% selected_gcms[[1]]$GCM) %>%
  left_join(selected_gcms[[1]], by = "GCM")

ggplot(all_delta_fireprob, aes(x = mean_runoff_in, y = delta_fp)) + geom_point()
```

Fire sensitivity:

Dillon, Gregory K. 2023. Wildfire Hazard Potential for the United States (270-m), version 2023. 4th Edition. Updated 17 July 2024. Fort Collins, CO: Forest Service Research Data Archive. <https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2015-0047-4>

The wildfire hazard potential (WHP) map is a raster geospatial product produced by the USDA Forest Service, Fire Modeling Institute that can help to inform evaluations of wildfire hazard or prioritization of fuels management needs across very large landscapes. Our specific objective with the WHP map is to depict the relative potential for high-intensity wildfire that may be difficult to manage. To create the 2023 version, we built upon spatial datasets of wildfire likelihood and intensity generated with the Large Fire Simulator (FSim), as well as spatial fuels and vegetation data from LANDFIRE 2020 and point locations of past fire occurrence (ca. 1992 - 2020). With these datasets as inputs, we produced an index of WHP for the United States at a 270-meter resolution. We present the WHP map in two forms: 1) continuous integer values, and 2) five WHP classes of very low, low, moderate, high, and very high. Areas mapped with higher WHP values represent fuels with a higher probability of experiencing torching, crowning, and other forms of extreme fire behavior under conducive weather conditions, based primarily on landscape conditions at the end of 2020.

This 2023 version of WHP was created from updated national wildfire hazard datasets of annual burn probability and fire intensity generated by the USDA Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station with the large fire simulation system (FSim). Vegetation and wildland fuels data from LANDFIRE 2020 (version 2.2.0) were the primary inputs to the updated FSim modeling work and therefore form the foundation for this version of the WHP. As such, the data presented here reflect landscape conditions as of the end of 2020. LANDFIRE 2020 vegetation and fuels data were also used directly in the WHP mapping process, along with updated point locations of fire occurrence ca. 1992-2020. With these datasets as inputs, we produced an index of WHP for all of the conterminous United States at 270-meter resolution. We present the final WHP map in two forms: 1) continuous integer values, and 2) five WHP classes of very low, low, moderate, high, and very high. On its own, WHP is not an explicit map of wildfire threat or risk, but when paired with spatial data depicting highly valued resources and assets such as structures or powerlines, it can approximate relative wildfire risk to those specific resources and assets. WHP is also not a forecast or wildfire outlook for any particular season, as it does not include any information on current or forecasted weather or fuel moisture conditions. It is instead intended for long-term strategic fuels management.

GRAB MEAN WATER SUPPLY RANKING OF CONTINUOUS WHP IN THE WATER SUPPLY PYROME:

```{r WHP}

# continuous fire hazard potential, cropped to water supply pyrome:
whp_cnt <- terra::rast("data/all/usfs_fire/whp2023_GeoTIF/whp2023_cnt_conus.tif") %>%
  terra::crop(., sf::st_transform(water_supply_pyromes, 5070), 
              mask = TRUE, touches = TRUE) %>%
  na.omit()

# transform the ranked values into percentiles (at 1 percent intervals):
values <- terra::values(whp_cnt, na.rm = TRUE)

quantiles <- quantile(values, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.01)) %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(to = c(lead(value, 1))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(to = ifelse(is.na(to), max(values) + 1, to)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(becomes = seq(0, 1, by = 0.01))

# Return the percentiles based on 1% threshold defined above
whp_quantiled <- terra::classify(whp_cnt, rcl = quantiles, right = TRUE)

# plot(whp_quantiled)

# grab percentiles within the water supply watershed:
water_supply_fire_potential <- whp_quantiled %>%
  crop(sf::st_transform(aoi, 5070), mask = TRUE) 

# calculate area-weightem mean of the water supply watershed:
mean_fire_potential <- terra::zonal(water_supply_fire_potential, 
                                    terra::vect(sf::st_transform(aoi, 5070)), fun = "mean", weights = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

# mapview(raster::raster(water_supply_fire_potential)) + watersupply_watershed
```

# 7. Drought (SPEI)

```{r spei}

# Calculate SPEI
# Calculate SPEI using the {spei} package

# This method allows control to summarize by 2 months or 6 months simply
# by changing ag_n to the aggregate #. 1 = monthly, 6 = 6 months.
ag_n <- 6 # number of months to aggregate for time series, 1 = monthly
freq <- 12/ag_n # frequency 
agg_months <- ifelse(ag_n == 1, paste0(ag_n, " month"), paste0(ag_n, " months"))

# Aggregate into ag_n dataframe
agg_wbm <- wbm %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                month = month(date),
                time_ag = floor_date(date, agg_months)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year, time_ag, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(precip_in_wbm = sum(precip_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean_C = mean(tmean_C, na.rm = TRUE),
                   pet_in_wbm = sum(pet_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   runoff_in_wbm = sum(runoff_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   discharge_gpm = mean(discharge_gpm, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(balance = precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm,
                month = month(time_ag)) %>% 
  ungroup()


# Grab last year of WBM data
end_year = agg_wbm$year %>% tail(n = 1)
end_month = agg_wbm$month %>% tail(n = 1)

# Calculate SPEI for Hot Dry and Warm Wet futures. Both require historical data
# so calculate separately then join
# Hot Dry
spei_drier <- agg_wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Historical", "Drier")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(spei = c(spei(ts(c(balance), 
                                         end = c(end_year, end_month), 
                                         frequency = freq),
                                      scale = freq,
                                      ref.end = c(2023, 1)) %>%
                                   .[["fitted"]])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = as.Date(paste0(year,"-",month,"-01")))

# Warm Wet
spei_wetter <- agg_wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Historical", "Wetter")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(spei = c(spei(ts(balance, 
                                          end = c(end_year, end_month), 
                                          frequency = freq), 
                           scale = freq,
                           ref.end = c(2023, 1)) %>%
                        .[["fitted"]])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = as.Date(paste0(year,"-",month,"-01")))

# Join
spei <- bind_rows(
  spei_drier %>% dplyr::filter(year >= 2024),
  spei_wetter
)


# Calculate Drought Metrics from SPEI

#' 1. Frequency and Duration of Drought Events: Threshold-Based Identification: 
#' Define drought events based on crossing a specific negative SPEI threshold 
#' (e.g., SPEI < -1 for moderate drought, SPEI < -1.5 for severe drought, 
#' SPEI < -2 for extreme drought). Frequency: Calculate the number of drought 
#' events occurring within a defined historical period and within different 
#' projected future periods (e.g., 2021-2050, 2051-2080, 2081-2100). Compare the 
#' frequency between historical and future periods. Duration: For each 
#' identified drought event, calculate its duration (number of consecutive 
#' months below the threshold). Compare the average or maximum drought duration 
#' between historical and future periods. You can also analyze the distribution 
#' of drought durations.


# Drought severity
spei_severity <- spei %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2065) %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(moderate = spei <= -1,
                severe = spei <= -1.5,
                extreme = spei <= -2) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(n = n(),
                   mod_percent = 100*sum(moderate, na.rm = TRUE)/n,
                   sev_percent = 100*sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE)/n,
                   ext_percent = 100*sum(extreme, na.rm =TRUE)/n,
                   mean_spei = mean(spei),
                   median_spei = median(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sd_spei = sd(spei, na.rm = TRUE))


# Drought frequency
spei_frequency <- spei %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(moderate = spei <= -1,
                severe = spei <= -1.5,
                extreme = spei <= -2) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mod_event = cumsum(moderate & !lag(moderate, default = FALSE)),
                sev_event = cumsum(severe & !lag(severe, default = FALSE)),
                ext_event = cumsum(extreme & !lag(extreme, default = FALSE)))

spei_metrics <- left_join(
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(moderate) %>%
  group_by(CF, mod_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mod_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)),
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(severe) %>%
  group_by(CF, sev_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(sev_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)), by = "CF") %>%
  left_join(
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(extreme) %>%
  group_by(CF, ext_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(ext_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)), by = "CF") %>%
  left_join(spei_severity, by = "CF") %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  row_to_names(row_number = 1) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Metric") %>%
  arrange(Metric)

# Alternative to consider later (thoughts)
#Transition Probabilities and Persistence: Markov Chain Analysis: Treat SPEI categories (e.g., non-drought, mild drought, moderate drought, etc.) as states in a Markov chain. Estimate the transition probabilities between these states based on the historical SPEI time series. Then, project future transition probabilities and compare them to the historical ones. An increase in the probability of transitioning to or staying in more severe drought categories indicates a higher risk of prolonged and intense drought. Analyze sequences of SPEI values below a certain threshold to identify drought "runs." Calculate the probability of a drought ending within a certain timeframe based on historical data and compare this to projections.



ggplot(spei %>% dplyr::filter(month(ym) == 7), aes(x = spei, y = discharge_gpm)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "SPEI", y = "MeanDischarge (GPM)") +
  scale_color_colorblind()
#  scale_y_log10()
```

# 5. Tables

##### Table 1

Magnitude statistics: Annual runoff, discharge, and recharge (inches) summary statistics for historical (H) and future (F) periods. % change = (F - H / H) of mean annual stat.

```{r table_1}
change <- wbm_annual %>%
  filter(year >= 1979 & year < 2065) %>%
  mutate(stat_group = ifelse(year < 2013, "Hist",
                             ifelse(year >= 2035, "Fut", "Present"))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(stat_group, CF, runoff_in_wbm, discharge_gpm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, stat_group) %>%
  dplyr::summarize_all(.funs = list(mean = mean, 
                                    #median = median, 
                                    sd = sd)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_group != "Present",
                !(stat_group == "Hist" & CF == "Drier"),
                !(stat_group == "Hist" & CF == "Wetter")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-stat_group) %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% # Convert to data frame (t() returns a matrix)
  set_names(.[1, ]) %>% # Set column names from the first row
  slice(-1)  %>% # Remove the first row (which now contains the column names)
  mutate(across(everything(), ~suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.))))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`% Change Drier` = 100 * (`Drier` - Historical) / Historical,
                `% Change Wetter` = 100 * (`Wetter` - Historical) / Historical) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), .fns = ~ signif(.x, 3)))
  

kable(change)
```

##### Table 3

Storage ratio (S-D)

Summary of water use, storage tank size, and storage to demand ratio

```{r table_3}
# # Storage:Demand Ratio
# TP <- c("Annual Mean", "Annual Max", "Summer Mean", "Summer Max")

storage_vol <- 153500 * gal_to_cf

SD <- monthly_use_long %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month_date = as.Date(month_date),
                month_days = days_in_month(month_date)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(period = ifelse(year(month_date) < 2012, "Historical", "Future")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(period) %>%
  dplyr::filter(mid_use == max(mid_use) |
                high_use == max(high_use)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(daily_use = 2 * mid_use / month_days,
                daily_use_high = 2 * high_use / month_days) %>%
  dplyr::mutate("Storage_cf" = storage_vol) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mid_use, high_use, daily_use, daily_use_high),
               names_to = "use_cat", values_to = "use") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SD = Storage_cf / use,
                use = use/1000,
                Storage_kcf = Storage_cf/1000,
                days_of_use = ifelse(grepl("daily", use_cat), SD, month_days * SD)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), .fns = ~ signif(.x, 2))) 


kable(SD)
```

```{r figure_3}
# Flow in Coal Creek and Mammoth Creek, the two nearest NWIS gauges to Blowhard Spring
f3 <- ggplot(nwis_select_discharge %>%
               dplyr::filter(year(date) > 1980) %>%
             dplyr::mutate(doy = yday(date),
                           time_per = ifelse(year(date) < 2000, "1980-2000", "2000-2025")) %>%
               dplyr::mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31")) %>%
              dplyr::group_by(doy_date, site_no, time_per) %>%
              dplyr::summarize(discharge_in = mean(discharge, na.rm = TRUE),
                               discharge_max = max(discharge, na.rm = TRUE),
                               discharge_min = min(discharge, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
               left_join(nwis_select_stream_gage, by = "site_no") %>%
               dplyr::mutate(site_name = gsub(" NEAR CEDAR CITY, UT", "", site_name),
                             site_name = gsub(" ABV WEST HATCH DITCH, NEAR HATCH, UT", "", site_name)) %>%
               dplyr::mutate(group_cat = paste0(site_name, " (",time_per, ")"),
                             group_cat = factor(group_cat,
                                                   levels = c("COAL CREEK (1980-2000)",
                                                              "COAL CREEK (2000-2025)",
                                                              "MAMMOTH CREEK (1980-2000)",
                                                              "MAMMOTH CREEK (2000-2025)"))),
                               aes(x = doy_date, y = discharge_in, color = group_cat)) +
  #geom_ribbon(aes(x = doy, ymax = discharge_max, ymin = discharge_min, fill = site_name), alpha = 0.2, lwd = 0) +
   geom_line(data = blowhard_mtn_d %>%
               dplyr::filter(year(date) > 1980) %>% 
         dplyr::mutate(doy = yday(date),
                       doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31")) %>%
         dplyr::group_by(doy_date) %>%
         dplyr::summarize(snwd = mean(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
                          snow = mean(snow, na.rm = TRUE)),
       aes(x = doy_date, y = snwd * 3.2, color = "BLOWHARD MOUNTAIN (1980-2006)"), lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(data = blowhard_mtn_d %>%
               dplyr::filter(year(date) < 1980) %>% 
         dplyr::mutate(doy = yday(date),
                       doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31")) %>%

         dplyr::summarize(snwd = mean(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
                          snow = mean(snow, na.rm = TRUE)),
       aes(x = doy_date, y = snwd * 3.2, color = "BLOWHARD MOUNTAIN (1964-1980)"), lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(lwd = 2, color = "black", aes(group = group_cat)) +

  scale_color_manual("", values = c(pal$lightpink, pal$pink, "lightblue", pal$darkblue, "gray90", "gray70")) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c(pal$lightpink, pal$darkpink, "lightblue", pal$darkblue)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Mean Daily Discharge (cfs)") +
   theme(legend.position = "bottom",
```

#### Water Budget

Plot of historical and projected annual water budget components for the contributing area of the proposed new well shown with a rolling 10-year average.

```{r wb_fig}
plot_dat <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(year,
                GCM,
                CF,
                "Precipitation (in)" = "precip_in_wbm",
                "Temperature (F)" = "tmean_F",
                "AET (in)" = "aet_in_wbm",
                "Snowmelt (in)" = "melt_in_wbm",
                "Rain (in)" = "rain_in_wbm",
                "Snow (in)" = "snow_in_wbm",
                "Discharge (gpm)" = "discharge_gpm",
                "Runoff (in)" = "runoff_in_wbm") %>%
                #"Discharge (in)" = "discharge_in_wbm",
                #"Recharge (in)" = "recharge_in_wbm") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(year, GCM, CF), names_to = "vars", values_to = "vals") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(vars, CF, GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(roll_vals = data.table::frollmean(vals, 10, align = c("center")))

wb_fig <- ggplot(plot_dat) + 
  # Add shaded region between 2035 and 2065
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 2035, xmax = 2065, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = vals, color = CF), lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, group = CF), 
            lineend = "round", color = "black", lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, color = CF),
            lineend = "round") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Historical" = "#a9a9a9", "Drier" = "#c5312a", "Wetter" = "#85b6dc")) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("#a9a9a9", "#c5312a","#85b6dc"),
                    labels = c("Historical", "Hot Dry", "Warm Wet")) +
  labs(y = "", x = "") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(vars, levels = c("Temperature (F)",
                                       "Precipitation (in)",
                                       "Rain (in)",
                                       "Snow (in)",
                                       "Snowmelt (in)",
                                       "AET (in)",
                                       "Runoff (in)",
                                       "Discharge (gpm)")),
             scales = "free", nrow = 2) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -20, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

wb_fig

ggsave(wb_fig, filename = "docs/Deep Dives/CEBR/Figs/WaterBalance.tif", width = 9, height = 5,  dpi = 600)
```

#### Annual Runoff Variability

Plot showing runoff variability for historical and future CFs.

```{r}

pdat <- wbm_annual %>%
         dplyr::filter(year < 2100) %>%
         dplyr::mutate(Runoff = 86400 * 365.25 * runoff_cfs_wbm) 
  

hist_median <- median(pdat[pdat$year < 2013,]$Runoff, na.rm = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()
hist_q_low <- quantile(pdat[pdat$year < 2013,]$Runoff, .1, na.rm = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()
hist_q_high <- quantile(pdat[pdat$year < 2013,]$Runoff, .9, na.rm = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()

runoff_var <- ggplot(pdat %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(Runoff), values_to = "vals", names_to = "vars") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rect_min = ifelse(CF != "Historical", 2035, 1979),
                rect_max = ifelse(CF != "Historical", 2065, 2012),
                CF = factor(CF,levels=c("Historical","Drier","Wetter")))) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = rect_min, xmax = rect_max, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = year, y = vals, fill = CF,
               group = vars), stat = "identity", width = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = hist_median, color = "Historical Median")) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = hist_q_low, color = "Historical 0.1 and 0.9 Quantile"), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = hist_q_high, color = "Historical 0.1 and 0.9 Quantile"), linetype = "dashed") +
 theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Runoff (CF)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = unit_format(unit = "M", scale = 1e-6)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("Historical" = "#a9a9a9", "Drier" = "#c5312a", "Wetter" = "#85b6dc")) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("gray30", pal$black, "gray30")) +
  facet_wrap(~CF, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(strip.background =element_rect(fill="gray95")) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(colour = 'black', face = "bold")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) 


runoff_var

# Calculate consecutive dry years
t <- pdat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2012 | (year >= 2035 & year < 2065)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(r_lt_p1 = ifelse(Runoff <= hist_q_low, 1,0),
                r_gt_p90 = ifelse(Runoff  >= hist_q_high, 1,0),
                tot = ifelse(Runoff > 0, 1)) %>%
     dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(r_lt_p1, r_gt_p90, tot, CF, Runoff,year)

hist_rle <- rle(t[t$CF == "Historical",]$r_lt_p1)
hist_rle_max <- hist_rle$lengths[hist_rle$values == 1] %>% max()

d_rle <- rle(t[t$CF == "Drier",]$r_lt_p1)
d_rle_max <- d_rle$lengths[d_rle$values == 1] %>% max()

w_rle <- rle(t[t$CF == "Wetter",]$r_lt_p1)
w_rle_max <- w_rle$lengths[w_rle$values == 1] %>% max(na.rm = TRUE)

# Get maximum runoff during each time period
max_run <- t %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(max_runoff = max(Runoff, na.rm = TRUE))

# Get percentage increase for warm wet max compared to historical max
max_run[max_run$CF == "Wetter",][[2]] / max_run[max_run$CF == "Historical",][[2]]

# Print summary of extreme wet and dry years
t %>%
    dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  summarize_all(.funs = c(mean = mean, sum = sum)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(lt_per = 100 * r_lt_p1_sum/tot_sum,
                gt_per = 100 * r_gt_p90_sum/tot_sum)


ggsave(runoff_var, filename = "docs/Deep Dives/CEBR/Figs/Runoff_Var.tif",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 3)

```

##### Precip Extreme Events

Frequency of extreme (p99) precipitation events.

```{r extreme_runoff_frequency}

df <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::rename(cf = CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cf) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rolling_3day = frollapply(precip_in_wbm, FUN = "sum", n = 3, align = "center"),
                date = as_date(date),
                year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(rolling_3day))

 df %>% dplyr::filter(year < 2070) %>% dplyr::group_by(cf) %>% dplyr::summarize(r = max(rolling_3day))

var = "precip_in_wbm"
q1 = 0.05 
q2 = 0.99

historic <- df %>%
  dplyr::filter(cf == "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::rename("variable" = var) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Explore runoff events ONLY:
  dplyr::filter(rolling_3day > 0,
                # AND only data from 1979-2012
                year >= hist_yrs[1] & year < hist_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::select(rolling_3day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(QLOW = quantile(rolling_3day, probs = as.numeric(q1)),
                   QHIGH = quantile(rolling_3day, probs = as.numeric(q2)))

year_counts <- df %>%
  dplyr::rename("variable" = var) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(low_day = ifelse(rolling_3day <= historic$QLOW, 1, 0),
                high_day = ifelse(rolling_3day >= historic$QHIGH, 1, 0)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cf, year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(n_low_days = sum(low_day),
                   n_high_days = sum(high_day)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(type = ifelse(cf == "Historical", "Historical", "Future"))

sanity_check <- df %>%
  dplyr::filter(rolling_3day >= historic$QHIGH)

stats_precip <- year_counts %>%
  dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year < hist_yrs[2] | year >= fut_yrs[1] & year < fut_yrs[2]) %>%
  group_by(cf) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(n_high_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(n_high_days, na.rm = TRUE))


xx <- ggplot(year_counts %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rect_min = ifelse(cf != "Historical", 2035, 1979),
                rect_max = ifelse(cf != "Historical", 2065, 2012),
                CF = factor(cf,levels=c("Historical","Drier","Wetter")))) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = rect_min, xmax = rect_max, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = year, y = n_high_days, fill = CF), stat = "identity", width = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
 theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number Precipitation Events ≥ p99") +
  #scale_y_continuous(labels = unit_format(unit = "M", scale = 1e-6)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("Historical" = "#a9a9a9", "Drier" = "#c5312a", "Wetter" = "#85b6dc")) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("gray30", pal$black, "gray30")) +
  facet_wrap(~CF, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(strip.background =element_rect(fill="gray95")) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(colour = 'black', face = "bold")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))



xx

ggsave(xx, filename = "docs/Deep Dives/CEBR/Figs/Extreme_Precip_events.jpg", dpi = 600, height = 3, width = 7.5)
```
